subject.title: feat(plugins): support per-agent plugin installation with --agent flag

question: Should OpenClaw accept this per-agent plugin installation contract in core now, and if so must it land as a complete install/update/uninstall/discovery/security lifecycle rather than install-only persistence?
rationale: This PR adds public CLI and persisted config surface for executable plugin code, so automation cannot choose the durable product/security contract without maintainer intent.

options.title: Require the full scoped lifecycle first
options.body: Keep the direction open but require normalized agent validation plus scoped install, uninstall, update, doctor, discovery/restart, and shared-state tests before merge.

options.title: Defer to the design issue
options.body: Close or pause this PR and continue the contract discussion in the linked issue until maintainers settle the product/security model.

options.title: Accept install-only as experimental
options.body: Maintainers may intentionally accept a partial surface, but they would own the upgrade and cleanup risk for scoped records created before lifecycle support exists.

recommendation.title: Require the full scoped lifecycle first
recommendation.body: Keep the direction open but require normalized agent validation plus scoped install, uninstall, update, doctor, discovery/restart, and shared-state tests before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent history across plugin install control-plane behavior and docs, and the decision spans CLI, config, and plugin lifecycle ownership.
